account-wide-agent-grant-01.graded_text: The design gives the agent connection a scope covering every workspace the person belongs to now or later plus documents shared with them individually, and does not make the person pick one organization per connection.

votes.e: A/project/docs/workspace-access.md:73 "Decision: one OAuth connection covers every workspace the person belongs to."; :63 "By default that is *all my workspaces*, which is derived live from membership, so joining a new client workspace needs no reconnect."; :103 list_documents searches "across all your workspaces and documents shared with you"; :75 rejects the organization-scoped grant "where consent selects one workspace and switching means re-authorizing".

account-wide-agent-grant-02.graded_text: Every tool call resolves the target workspace or document and checks live membership, role, and individual share on the server at call time. A single organization claim in a token is not treated as proof of access to any other workspace.

votes.e: A/project/docs/workspace-access.md:73 "Each tool call names the workspace or document it acts on, and the gate checks membership for that specific target on that call."; :17 "Roles, membership, and agent reach are read live at each call."; :81 "If the token carries an organization claim, it is **ignored for authorization**. It never selects or limits a workspace."; :65 allowed = (role grants it OR share grants it) AND scope AND policy AND reach.

account-wide-agent-grant-03.graded_text: The create tool takes an explicit destination workspace ID, and the server verifies the caller may create in that workspace before creating. The design does not say a client-supplied workspace ID must never be used.

votes.e: A/project/docs/workspace-access.md:115 "`workspace` is **required** and takes a workspace ID ... an omitted workspace is a validation error, not a silent fallback."; server check via :65 and :174 "`authorize(principal, capability, target)` ... inside the same backend transaction that reads or writes" with :53 role table (create: Owner/Editor yes, Viewer no) and :128 refusal "You are a Viewer in Acme Studio, so you can read but not edit or create there." Nowhere says a client workspace ID must never be used; :14 "Which workspace or document is addressed comes from the request ... a tool argument. Selecting never grants."

account-wide-agent-grant-04.graded_text: Removing a membership or an individual share takes effect for an already connected agent without reconnecting.

votes.e: A/project/docs/workspace-access.md:83 "Removing someone from a workspace cuts their agent off from it on the very next call, because membership is read live."; shares go through the same per-call gate (:65 "(role grants it OR share grants it)") under :17 "Nothing is cached as a grant that a later change could leave stale." Share removal is covered only by this general rule, not named explicitly.

account-wide-agent-grant-05.graded_text: An individually shared document gives access to that document only, never to its workspace's other documents or member list, through the UI and the agent alike.

votes.e: A/project/docs/workspace-access.md:57 "A share grants exactly one document to exactly one person ... It never grants `workspace.list`, `document.create`, `document.share`, or sight of any other document in that workspace."; agent side :103 "`workspace` is `null` for share-only documents, so the agent never learns workspace details the person cannot see"; UI :147 "`/w/<id>/members` | Workspace members (Owner/Editor see it ...)", :160 "Share-only documents are matched on their own content only."

account-wide-agent-grant-06.graded_text: The library shows documents from every workspace the person belongs to by default, with workspace and shared filters held in URL query state, filters only narrow what is shown, and no active-workspace session state is introduced as an authority for browsing or for the agent connection.

votes.e: A/project/docs/workspace-access.md:144 "`/documents` | The library: every document the person can reach, across all workspaces and shares"; :158 "Filters, in this URL order: `q` (search), `workspace=<id>` (one workspace), `shared=true` ..."; :103 "`workspace` is an optional filter that only narrows a read"; :138 "the app has no 'current workspace' state"; :15 "There is no active workspace in session state, cookies, client memory, or token claims that decides where a write lands."

account-wide-agent-grant-07.graded_text: The design introduces no per-seat price and no paid seat gate, and leaves the member cap of 25 as the brief states it. A design that does not discuss billing or the cap passes.

votes.e: Checked A/project/docs/workspace-access.md and A/diff.txt; no seat price or seat gate. Closest line :181 "offers an upgrade to the Owner" is a storage upgrade, matching the brief's storage pricing. Cap left as stated, :182 "**Member cap 25** is the same on every plan ... No upgrade is offered at the cap, because no plan raises it."

account-wide-agent-grant-08.graded_text: The design says the consent screen states the connection's scope, including workspaces joined later.

votes.e: Checked A/project/docs/workspace-access.md and A/answer.txt for consent-screen content. The only mention of consent is :75 "the usual pattern of an organization-scoped grant, where consent selects one workspace", which describes the rejected alternative. Nothing says the consent screen states that the connection reaches all current workspaces and ones joined later; :63 puts the reach only in account settings after connecting.

blocking: [claude-fallback] A/project/docs/workspace-access.md:80 "Audience is enforced only if the provider actually mints one (check a real token before writing the check, and say in code why it is conditional)." It does not commit to audience binding. Built as written, the MCP server could accept an access token minted for another client or resource on the same provider instance, and that token would then reach every one of the person's workspaces under the account-wide grant (:85).

[claude-fallback] A/project/docs/workspace-access.md:115 marks create_document "not idempotent", and :204 leaves "Should `create_document` accept an idempotency key so an agent's retry does not create a duplicate?" as an open question. Agents retry calls, so building it as written creates duplicate documents.

[claude-fallback] A/project/docs/workspace-access.md:111 update_document is a full content replace, and :203 "Should `update_document` take an expected version to avoid an agent overwriting a person's concurrent edit? Not designed here." Under concurrency, an agent write silently overwrites a person's edit.
